characterized_levers.name: Technical Feasibility Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Demonstrating technical feasibility impacts policy. Immediate: Demonstrators built → Systemic: 15% increased policy traction due to concrete evidence → Strategic: Enhanced credibility in procurement negotiations.
options: Focus demonstrator efforts on a single, highly secure authentication method, such as FIDO2, on a mainstream Android device.
Develop demonstrators for both FIDO2 on GrapheneOS and a browser-based fallback, accepting slightly longer development timelines.
Explore passwordless authentication via blockchain-anchored identity and decentralized identifiers (DIDs) alongside FIDO2 and browser-based fallback demonstrators.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Technical Risk vs. Scope. Weakness: The options don't explicitly address the cost implications of each demonstrator approach.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on demonstrating technical feasibility to impact policy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of the technical demonstrators on policy traction, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to demonstrator development.
characterized_levers.description: Technical Feasibility Strategy maps, validates, and communicates the technical boundaries of a platform-neutral or fallback authentication approach for Denmark’s digital identity project. It controls demonstrator scope and rigor, selects prototype modalities (e.g., FIDO2/WebAuthn on GrapheneOS, a browser-based fallback, and hardware-token workflows), and defines success metrics such as demonstrator maturity, interoperability with open standards, and credible implications for procurement language and cost estimates. Key indicators include cross-method functionality, resilience against spoofing, alignment with NSIS/eIDAS constraints, development cadence, and the ability to translate technical findings into policy-relevant risk and cost inputs for decision-makers.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Synergy with Policy Advocacy Strategy and Coalition Building Strategy is strongest: credible demonstrators ground policy proposals and coalition messages, boosting procurement discussions and accountability. It also informs EU Standards Engagement Strategy by clarifying what interoperability requirements are technically achievable. This integration helps ensure rollout realism across levers.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Potential conflicts emerge when narrowed demonstrator choices reduce broad stakeholder buy-in (affecting Coalition Building Strategy) or when technical signals lag EU standards timelines (framing conflicts with EU Standards Engagement Strategy). These tensions can constrain Procurement Influence Strategy by signaling higher risk to suppliers and complicating bid language.

characterized_levers.name: Policy Advocacy Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Policy advocacy shapes procurement. Immediate: Policy proposals submitted → Systemic: 20% greater likelihood of influencing AltID requirements → Strategic: Increased adoption of platform-neutral standards.
options: Focus advocacy on continuity of service and supplier concentration risks, avoiding direct privacy arguments.
Balance continuity arguments with privacy and democratic accountability concerns, broadening the coalition.
Prioritize open-source governance and community-led development models for digital identity, framing platform neutrality as a public good.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Political Risk vs. Coalition Size. Weakness: The options don't consider the potential for regulatory capture by incumbent vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on policy advocacy shaping procurement, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of policy advocacy on influencing AltID requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to advocacy focus.
characterized_levers.description: Policy Advocacy Strategy orchestrates the framing, timing, and political channeling of arguments for platform-neutral access, fallback authentication, and procurement neutrality. It defines messaging, targets Digitaliseringsstyrelsen, parliamentary committees, and partner NGOs, translates technical demonstrator results into policy proposals, risk assessments, and regulatory asks. Objectives include securing formal policy proposals, increasing resilience discourse in procurement, and shaping contract language to favor platform-neutrality. Success metrics include policy submissions, formal engagement milestones, and measurable shifts in decision-makers' stated expectations. The strategy coordinates with other levers to ensure policy proposals reflect demonstrator experience and stakeholder needs.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Strong synergy with Coalition Building Strategy and EU Standards Engagement Strategy: policy narratives grounded in demonstrator findings amplify civil-society voices, while EU-aligned messaging enhances procurement and interoperability discussions. This cross-lever collaboration increases the likelihood that AltID-related documents incorporate platform-neutral requirements.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Conflicts may arise when policy timetables collide with coalition dynamics (slowing consensus) or when prioritizing privacy and democratic accountability narrows procurement language. It can conflict with Coalition Building Strategy if messaging fractures under divergent stakeholder views, and with EU Standards Engagement Strategy if national policy lags EU standards progression.

characterized_levers.name: Coalition Building Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Coalition strength amplifies advocacy. Immediate: Stakeholder engagement increased → Systemic: 30% stronger advocacy position in procurement discussions → Strategic: Greater political pressure for platform neutrality.
options: Build a narrow coalition focused on security experts and contingency-planning stakeholders.
Expand the coalition to include civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, and academic researchers.
Actively recruit dissenting voices from within the MitID operator and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen to foster internal debate.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Speed vs. Breadth of Support. Weakness: The options fail to address the potential for conflicting priorities within the coalition.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on coalition building to amplify advocacy, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of coalition strength on advocacy position, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to coalition composition.
characterized_levers.description: Coalition Building Strategy aims to broaden support beyond technical specialists to civil-society organizations, privacy advocates, academic researchers, contingency-planning stakeholders, and sympathetic policymakers. It coordinates outreach and messaging to maintain momentum, manages competing priorities, and channels input into policy and procurement discussions. The objective is to build a credible, diverse coalition that can exert political pressure for platform neutrality and resilience. Immediate engagement growth, formal endorsements, and stronger signals in procurement deliberations define success. It also requires governance structures and clear roles to avoid fragmentation. Regular coordination mechanisms and conflict-resolution processes are part of the plan.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Strong synergy with Policy Advocacy Strategy and EU Standards Engagement Strategy: a broad coalition strengthens policy messaging, aligns national and EU conversations, and expands credibility in procurement and standards forums. It also provides diverse risk perspectives to inform demonstrator scope and procurement language.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Conflicts arise when coalition breadth slows decisions or introduces competing priorities, affecting speed and focus. It may conflict with Policy Advocacy Strategy if messaging fractures under divergent voices, and with EU Standards Engagement Strategy if national priorities lag EU standardization timelines.

characterized_levers.name: Procurement Influence Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: Procurement influence drives adoption. Immediate: Platform-neutral language included in procurement documents → Systemic: 25% faster scaling through mandated supplier diversity → Strategic: Reduced long-term dependency on Apple and Google.
options: Focus on including general language about supplier concentration risk in AltID procurement documents.
Advocate for specific requirements for platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication paths.
Propose a 'digital sovereignty bonus' in procurement scoring, rewarding vendors who demonstrably reduce platform dependency.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Specificity vs. Implementability. Weakness: The options don't account for the potential for vendors to game the procurement process.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on procurement influence driving adoption, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of procurement influence on scaling, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to procurement language.
characterized_levers.description: Procurement Influence Strategy defines how the project shapes procurement language, contract criteria, and vendor requirements to embed platform-neutral access and certified fallback authentication. It seeks to codify platform-diversity in AltID procurement documents, define fallback eligibility, and incentivize vendor capabilities through procurement scoring. The objective is to accelerate adoption while reducing long-term dependency on Apple and Google. Key success metrics include platform-neutral clauses in RFI/RFPs, an increase in bid diversity, and faster procurement cycles. It also aligns procurement language with EU standards and resilience goals.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Strong synergy with Technical Feasibility Strategy and Coalition Building Strategy: credible demonstrators inform bid language and evaluation criteria, while a broad coalition supports fair vendor evaluation and diversification in responses. This alignment also assists EU Standards Engagement Strategy by translating standards into executable procurement criteria.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Conflicts arise when procurement complexity invites vendor gaming or when requirements outpace demonstrator readiness. It may conflict with Technical Feasibility Strategy if procurement demands outstrip demonstrator capabilities, and with EU Standards Engagement Strategy if EU requirements impose constraints that are costly or difficult to verify within national procurement cycles.

characterized_levers.name: EU Standards Engagement Strategy
characterized_levers.consequences: EU standards engagement creates broader impact. Immediate: Input provided to relevant EU bodies → Systemic: 10% increased alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements → Strategic: Enhanced interoperability and reduced lock-in across Europe.
options: Monitor relevant EU bodies and technical working groups, providing occasional input on interoperability.
Actively engage with EU bodies, advocating for platform-neutral access and certified fallback mechanisms in eIDAS2 and related standards.
Champion a 'sovereign identity sandbox' within the EU Digital Identity Wallet framework to test and validate platform-neutral authentication models.
characterized_levers.review: Controls Resource Allocation vs. Scope of Influence. Weakness: The options don't address the potential for EU standards to be influenced by large platform vendors.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: This lever focuses on EU standards engagement creating broader impact, quantifying the impact. It is distinct because it quantifies the impact of EU standards engagement on alignment with European Digital Identity Wallet requirements, unlike other levers. It also has specific options related to EU engagement strategies.
characterized_levers.description: EU Standards Engagement Strategy coordinates Denmark's participation in EU standards bodies and technical working groups to align national digital identity plans with Europe-wide interoperability and resilience. It monitors eIDAS2, NSIS, and wallet frameworks, channels Danish input into EU discussions, and translates EU standards into national procurement and policy language. The strategy aims to reduce platform lock-in, promote platform-neutrality, and ensure fallback mechanisms meet European requirements for continuity of service. Success metrics include formal EU feedback, adoption of platform-neutral language in EU documents, and strengthened cross-border interoperability.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Strong synergy with Policy Advocacy Strategy and Coalition Building Strategy: aligning national work with EU standards strengthens domestic policy messaging, broadens coalition support, and improves cross-border procurement and interoperability discussions. It also informs Procurement Influence Strategy by providing EU-aligned criteria for tender specs.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Conflicts may occur when EU standards progress outpace national timelines, creating tension with Policy Advocacy Strategy and Coalition Building Strategy if messaging or consensus lags; it can complicate Procurement Influence Strategy if EU requirements impose constraints that are costly or difficult to verify.
